questions.q: What does dynamic data masking protect, compared to a row access policy?
options: Columns — it returns a masked or real value depending on the querying role
Whole tables — it blocks queries entirely for unprivileged roles
Warehouses — it limits which warehouse a role can use
Databases — it hides entire databases from the object browser
questions.explain: Row access policies filter which rows come back; masking policies work at the column level, substituting a masked value at query time based on the querying role.

questions.q: When a masking policy hides a value, what happens to the actual data stored on disk?
options: Nothing changes — the stored value is untouched; only the query result is masked
The real value is permanently overwritten with the masked version
Snowflake deletes the column and recreates it hourly
The table is automatically converted to a secure view
questions.explain: Masking happens at query time only. The underlying stored value never changes — the same SELECT returns the real value to a privileged role and a masked value to everyone else.

questions.q: Which statement actually attaches a masking policy to a specific column?
options: ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... SET MASKING POLICY
CREATE MASKING POLICY alone, with no further steps
GRANT MASKING POLICY TO ROLE
UPDATE TABLE ... APPLY MASK
questions.explain: CREATE MASKING POLICY only defines the logic. ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... SET MASKING POLICY is the step that actually attaches it to a column.

questions.q: In this lesson's ssn_mask example, what does a role that is NOT HR_ADMIN see when it queries the ssn column?
options: Everything but the last four characters replaced with asterisks
The complete, unmasked SSN value
An empty string with no value at all
A query error blocking the SELECT entirely
questions.explain: The CASE logic returns the full value only for HR_ADMIN; every other role falls into the ELSE branch, which returns '***-**-' concatenated with the last four characters.

questions.q: Why can a single masking policy be reused across many tables?
options: Because it's defined independently of any table, and can be attached to any column that shares the same sensitive data type
Because Snowflake automatically applies every masking policy to every table in the account
Because masking policies can only ever be attached to one column, so reuse is required
It cannot be reused — a new policy must be written for every column
questions.explain: CREATE MASKING POLICY defines the logic once, separately from any table, so the same policy (e.g. for every SSN column) can be attached wherever it's needed via ALTER TABLE.
